- What we heard on the call: expected traffic of ~10–50M tokens/month for the initial pilot (peaks during market hours), target p95 latency ~150ms for interactive flows, and preferred pilot budget band of $12k–$25k/month.

Open items for you to confirm (so I can put together a short quote and pilot plan):
1) Target tokens/mo you want us to price to (closest single number in that 10–50M range).
2) Any strict requirements on data residency or encryption (KMS/HSM) for the pilot.
3) Will procurement need an NDA/PO before a quote?

What I'm going to run next: unit-econ estimate for Hosted Premium (streaming) vs Dedicated reserved capacity with an example cost table for 10M / 20M / 50M tokens. Also capture latency tradeoffs: streaming + small batching for lowest p95 vs larger batching / cheaper model variants for aggressive cost savings.

Attaching the latest pricing sheet and a short SLO playbook so you can see tradeoffs.

Appreciate the recap, Marissa. A few clarifications from our side to make sure the quote focuses on what matters:

- Tokens: our likely pilot footprint is 20M tokens/month (with burst capacity up to ~50M in market-moving days).
- Budget: procurement has signaled a pilot budget in the $12k–$25k/month range. Ideally we want to see options that land at the lower end of that band if they don't materially impact latency.
- Target unit economics: as a rule of thumb the product team is targeting <$500 per 1M tokens for the pilot (closer to $300–$400 is ideal).
- Latency: product requires interactive experience — target p95 <= 150ms. If hitting that SLO requires a higher unit cost we need to see the delta and an explanation of why.
- Streaming: open to streaming for chat flows, but would like to understand price delta vs non-streaming (and whether streaming materially increases cost).

Procurement is copied for any immediate questions on terms/PO/NDA. Please include any recommended fallback policies (cheaper model variants, region fallback) and what that would do to unit costs.

Thanks,
Ethan Lau
Head of Product, FintechAI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FintechAI — cost & latency follow-up (post-call recap)

Thanks Ethan — super helpful. Per your asks below, high-level recommendations and example math (all numbers are estimates; I will include a formal quote after you confirm tokens/month and residency):

1) Hosted Premium (recommended if you want fastest time-to-value + SLO-backed latency):
   - Recommended config: Streaming enabled for chat paths, small batch window (30–50ms), prefix KV caching for repeated prompts.
   - Unit price example (p95 <= 150ms target): ~$450 per 1M tokens (includes model runtime, SLO overhead, and streaming cost).
   - Example: 20M tokens/month -> ~$9,000 / month. 50M tokens/month -> ~$22,500 / month.

2) Dedicated Reserved (recommended if you want lower marginal $/1M at scale and stable latency):
   - Reserved commit + burst pool; price depends on commit level. With a 12-month commit we can get unit economics down to ~$220 per 1M tokens (model-dependent).
   - Example (20M tokens/mo at $220/1M) -> ~$4,400 / month; 50M -> ~$11,000 / month.

3) Streaming vs non-streaming cost delta:
   - Streaming adds marginal CPU/transport overhead but is mainly an operational SLO/design choice. In Hosted, streaming adds ~10–20% premium to per‑token cost when compared to equivalent non-streaming config at the same latency. In Dedicated, premium is smaller (~5–10%).

4) Fallback / SLO-driven pricing:
   - We can configure an automatic fallback policy: primary model (higher cost) for interactive requests, and a compatible cheaper variant for bulk/low-priority workloads. When fallback is active, unit cost for those requests drops ~30–40% depending on model variant.

Next steps I propose: you confirm the target tokens/mo (20M looks like the right baseline) and whether you prefer Hosted pilot or a small Dedicated proof-of-concept (we can spin a 1–3 week Dedicated pilot with monitoring if you want to validate the $/1M math). I'll send a two-option quote (Hosted Premium streaming vs Dedicated 6-mo commit example) and a short pilot plan.

I've attached an SLA draft and the short SLO playbook for your review.

Attachments: SLA-draft.docx, SLO_playbook.pdf

Best,
Marissa

Quick note from infra/ops perspective: we can support an SLO-driven pricing rule that ties model selection + routing to latency budgets. Practical example:

- Primary route: lowest-latency variant (p95 <= 150ms) served from Premium pool.
- Fallback route: compatible, more quantized variant (p95 ~250–300ms) that reduces token cost by ~30%.
- Routing policy: traffic over X QPS or when queueing latency climbs will route % of non-critical requests to fallback automatically; this keeps interactive SLOs intact while lowering overall $/1M.

I'll include an ops checklist for pilot (telemetry hooks we need, and the policy knobs we'll expose in the Console). Happy to run a short simulation on our infra to show expected unit-cost delta if you'd like.

-Rishi
Principal Product Manager, Infra
